blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that bound_signer(binding, push_mode=None) leaves current_push_mode() == None (env/config fallback), distinct from push_mode='off' which forces 'off'.
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_binding.py:69 `push = push_mode if binding is not None else None`
Docstring claim (added): 'push_mode=None binds the SIGNER without overriding the push policy — the enclosed block signs from binding but the outbound push still falls back to the env/config default'
test file calls `with bound_signer(binding, push_mode=None):` (tests/unit/test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py:173, :215) but never asserts current_push_mode()

ABSENCE: search of tests/ for current_push_mode() finds only tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py:131-133 which asserts the OLD push=='off' path; no test asserts the new None-fallthrough for a bound signer
blocking.finding: The newly-added push_mode=None semantic in bound_signer (bind the signer but leave the push policy to fall back to the env/config default, so the box still auto-pushes) is exercised by the new tests but never asserted. No test reads current_push_mode() to confirm that bound_signer(binding, push_mode=None) leaves the push policy at None (env/config fallback) rather than forcing 'off'. Inverting the added line `push = push_mode if binding is not None else None` to always bind 'off' would leave every test in test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py green, so the specific behavior this diff introduces — the box auto-pushing its ticket writes while signing under the box env — is regression-blind.
scenarios: A refactor forcing push_mode='off' for the MCP binding (regressing the auto-push requirement) passes all tests
The box silently stops pushing its ticket writes to the shared store while all tests remain green
blocking.suggested_fix: In the goose test file, inside a `with bound_signer(binding, push_mode=None):` block assert `current_push_mode() is None`, and add a contrast asserting `current_push_mode() == 'off'` under `push_mode='off'`.
